name: ct-edit
description: Find/replace across files chosen by ct-search-style predicates, framed as a self-checking edit. It computes every replacement first, classifies the total against --expect into a SUCCESS/ERROR verdict, and writes ONLY when the verdict is SUCCESS and --dry-run is not set; otherwise nothing is written. Replacements preserve every untouched byte (line terminators, indentation, surrounding text): a CRLF file is written back CRLF, an LF file LF, a missing final newline stays missing, and new lines take the ending of the lines around them; --eol lf|crlf rewrites the endings of the files a run writes. --find/--replace accept payload schemes: file:PATH reads the value verbatim from a file (never promoted; literal by default), stdin: reads standard input, b64:DATA decodes base64 (the shell-safe way to carry backticks, $, quotes and newlines INLINE on one command line with no heredoc, pipe or scratch file), text:VALUE escapes the prefix. A single-line --find is matched per line and read as LITERAL text by default, because an anchor is a piece of code and code is full of ( ) [ ] . ? | *; --mode regex or --mode glob asks for the other readings, and --mode auto restores substring->glob->regex promotion. --mode applies to EVERY pattern in the invocation, so absent it --name still promotes as a glob while --find stays literal. When an anchor genuinely is not unique, --nth N applies only the Nth match in selection order (files in walk order, then top to bottom) and --at FILE:LINE applies only the match starting there; both imply --expect '=1', and a pick that lands on nothing reports where the anchor did match. A MULTI-LINE find payload matches as a line-anchored literal block (K lines match K consecutive source lines byte-for-byte; the replace payload's lines replace the block, an empty replace deletes it; a failed block reports its nearest miss: best-aligned candidate and first diverging line). With a regex --find, $1/${name} expand in --replace (use $$ for literal $); otherwise the replacement is literal. --script PATH runs a .ctb batch atomically under the prepare/confirm/write standard; --script b64:DATA carries the whole script inline on one command line (file:/stdin:/text: also accepted). Items: '#% edit expect="=1" mode=literal file=...' with '#% find' / '#% replace' (expect defaults to =1 in scripts; an empty replace deletes); '#% insert-before' / '#% insert-after' with '#% find' / '#% text' put text on the lines before/after each anchor match, naming the anchor once and leaving it in place; '#% drop' with '#% find' deletes each match's whole lines (a single-line find deletes every matching line, leaving no blank); '#% append' / '#% prepend' with '#% text' add lines at the end/start of the file and count one per file touched (so with =1 they need file= or an expect=). '#% end' closes an item. The whole script is simulated in memory first (cascade: each edit sees earlier edits' output; --no-cascade matches pristine and rejects overlap), every changed file is pre-flighted for writability, and nothing is written unless EVERY edit passes — no flag permits a partial write. --base is repeatable, so one script can touch two trees in one atomic run; per-item file= narrows within the whole selection. Only regular UTF-8 text files are edited. Not subject to the ct-test command allowlist (it runs no programs); safety is via --dry-run, --expect, atomicity, and your VCS. With --json emits {tool, verdict, dry_run, applied, replacements, files_changed, sites:[{path,line,before,after}]}; script runs emit per-edit results {ordinal, op, expect, mode (null for append/prepend), replacements, verdict, sites, nearest_miss?}. Exit: 0 SUCCESS, 1 ERROR, 2 usage/runtime error. Invoke as `ct edit ...` or `ct-edit ...`.

base.description: Roots to edit (repeatable). A file edits just that file; a directory is descended. Every --base joins one selection, so a script can touch two trees in one atomic run. Default ['.'].

name.description: Limit to files whose name matches; '|'-separated alternatives, each substring->glob->regex promoted and anchored to the whole name.

hidden.description: Include dot-entries (names starting with '.'). Default: skipped.

find.description: Anchor to find, matched per line and read as LITERAL text unless --mode says otherwise (an anchor is a piece of code: ( ) [ ] . ? | * are matched as themselves). Accepts file:PATH / stdin: / b64:DATA / text:VALUE payloads; a multi-line payload matches as a line-anchored literal block. Required unless script is given.

replace.description: Replacement text. With a regex --find (--mode regex, or --mode auto promoting to one), $1/${name} expand (use $$ for literal $); otherwise literal. Accepts file:PATH / stdin: / b64:DATA / text:VALUE; for a block find, an empty payload deletes the matched lines. Required unless script is given.

mode.description: How patterns are interpreted. literal|glob|regex pin one reading for every pattern in the invocation; auto states the substring->glob->regex promotion rule out loud. Use literal for verbatim code anchors.

nth.description: Apply only the Nth match (1-based) in selection order: files in walk order, then top to bottom within a file. For a non-unique anchor, when capturing a whole distinguishing block first would be overkill. Implies --expect '=1'; mutually exclusive with --at and --script.

at.description: Apply only the match starting at FILE:LINE, where FILE may be a whole-component path suffix (cli/ct_edit.rs) and LINE is 1-based. Pairs with `ct search --grep ... --detail`, whose path:line:text rows name the site directly. Implies --expect '=1'; mutually exclusive with --nth and --script.

squeeze-blank.description: Blank-line tolerant block matching: a maximal run of blank (empty or whitespace-only) lines in a multi-line --find matches a run of one-or-more blank lines in the source, regardless of count. No effect on a single-line --find or on --replace. In scripts, set per-edit squeeze=true instead.

script.description: Run a .ctb edit script: a batch of edit / insert-before / insert-after / drop / append / prepend items simulated and judged in full before any write; nothing is written unless every item passes. A bare value is a path; b64:DATA carries the whole script inline on one shell-safe command line, and file:PATH / stdin: / text:VALUE are accepted too.

fence.description: Directive prefix for script lines. Default '#%'; change it for payloads containing '#%' at line start.

no-cascade.description: Script edits match pristine content instead of cascading; overlapping edits become a usage error.

expect.description: Verdict expectation over the total replacement count; default 'any', or '=1' under --nth/--at (in scripts, per-edit expect= defaults to '=1'). One of: any (>=1), none (==0), N (>=N), =N (==N), +N (>N), -N (<N). The edit is written only if the verdict is SUCCESS.

eol.description: Line endings for the files this run writes: keep (each file's own, the default), lf, or crlf. Only files the edit changes are written, so an untouched file is never re-terminated.

dry-run.description: Compute and show the change and verdict, but write nothing.

quiet.description: Suppress the per-site diff; print only the summary line.

json.description: Emit a structured JSON result instead of text.

timeout.description: Abort with exit 2 (and a one-line message) if the scan exceeds SECS seconds (fractional allowed). Never interrupts the write phase: once a SUCCESS verdict starts writing, every write completes.

heartbeat.description: Print a liveness pulse every SECS seconds (fractional allowed) while the run is in progress.

heartbeat-emit.description: Heartbeat line template. Tokens: {ELAPSED} (whole seconds so far) {TOOL}. Default: "[{ELAPSED}s]".

heartbeat-to.description: Stream heartbeat pulses are written to. Default: stderr.

no-ignore.description: Walk gitignored / .ignore files too (the .git directory is always skipped); by default the walk skips what git would.

examples.why: Preview a rename across Rust sources before writing, instead of sed -i 's/foo_bar/foo_baz/g'.

examples.cmd: ct edit --base src --find 'let v = compute' --replace 'let w = compute' --at a.rs:13 --dry-run
examples.why: Change one site of a repeated anchor by position, taken straight from a ct search --detail row; --at implies --expect =1.
Rename in one file, refusing the write unless exactly the expected number of sites change.
